clue.text: Cherubic entitlements call for redress

parts.note: a putto is a cherub figure in Renaissance art, so the cherubic thing is a putto
entitlements are rights one can claim

explanation.surface: Angels demanding their due cry out for compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cherubic' reads as an adjective but stands for PUTTO, the chubby winged child of Italian painting; 'call for' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to correct it or set it straight again.

clue.text: Wrought up pigs splashed around in the mud

definitions.meaning: puddling is the furnace process that turned pig iron into wrought iron
made a muddy mess, as of water pools

explanation.surface: Agitated pigs wallowed noisily in the mire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests excited farm animals; the first sense is metallurgy, where pigs are ingots of crude iron worked up into wrought iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron so treated was converted in a furnace, and a pool trodden by feet becomes muddied water.

clue.text: Silver not all returned to a Polynesian kingdom

indicators.note: every piece of the phrase is read backwards from the end

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some of the silver failed to come back to an island monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all returned' turns AG and NOT together, giving TON then GA; 'not all' looks like 'some', but 'not' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific island nation is the last monarchy among the South Sea states.

clue.text: High time for a pilot to bank

definitions.meaning: high meat or milk is starting to go off

definitions.text: time for a pilot to bank
definitions.meaning: an aircraft banks while it changes direction

explanation.surface: A pilot judges the right moment to tilt the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' here means smelly, beginning to spoil, as milk does when it is about to sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Food beginning to sour is said to be going off, and a banking plane is mid-manoeuvre changing heading.

clue.text: The Oxford Thames has a pair of islands

indicators.note: two of something, so the abbreviation is written twice over

parts.note: Is is the standard abbreviation for island or islands

explanation.surface: The river through Oxford contains a couple of islets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford the stretch of the Thames is traditionally called the Isis.
explanation.definitionFit: Locally the river flowing past the university city goes by this name.

clue.text: It is almost too late for the first 2 words of 3

definitions.meaning: said when something should already have happened
the clue for 3-down begins '...'

explanation.surface: Nearly overdue, someone points to the opening of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is literal: the clue for 3-down opens with these two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom urging that something is overdue and should happen now.

clue.text: Bright and well honed

definitions.meaning: clever, quick-witted
with a keen cutting edge

explanation.definitionFit: A clever person is quick-witted, and a blade honed well has a keen edge.

clue.text: Rushed around the green of course and got soaked

indicators.note: the word for rushed is placed about the golf term

parts.note: rushed means sped
the tee is the patch of grass on a golf course where each hole starts

explanation.surface: A golfer dashed about the course and was drenched by rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests the putting green, but the tee is the turf area of a golf course where play begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steeped has been left immersed in liquid until saturated.

clue.text: No stamp needed …

parts.note: an envelope that may be mailed without paying for its delivery

explanation.surface: A letter that can be sent without paying postage.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to 14-down, whose answer is a synonym pair for this one's two words (stake, out).
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent at no charge to the sender carries no postage requirement.

clue.text: Finished job according to normal practice

parts.note: finished means done
a job is a task or thing to do

explanation.surface: Work completed in the usual manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to' only links the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means conventional, socially accepted behaviour.

clue.text: In total agreement an hour afternoon

definitions.meaning: united in opinion
one o'clock, sixty minutes past noon

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees on a meeting just after midday.
explanation.definitionFit: People in full harmony are united; one hour past noon is one o'clock on the clock.

clue.text: Though too lazy to work he presumably makes dough

definitions.text: Though too lazy to work he presumably makes dough

parts.words: Though too lazy to work he presumably makes dough
parts.note: an idler, read jokingly as a baker who produces loaves of bread

explanation.surface: A layabout somehow still earns money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' is slang for money and also bread mix; the idler's name reads as one who makes loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle person who lounges about is a layabout, punningly a bread-maker.

clue.text: Get a move on to terrace the garden maybe

definitions.meaning: hurry up, increase the pace
build stair levels up a sloping plot

explanation.surface: Hurry up and landscape that sloping lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Increasing effort means going faster, and terracing makes a slope into raised levels like stairs.

clue.text: Argument resulting from use of a carpet sweeper?

definitions.meaning: a quarrel or brawl

definitions.text: resulting from use of a carpet sweeper?
definitions.meaning: what a sweeper raises from the rug

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over who does the hoovering.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle or fight is informally a row; sweeping stirs particles off the floor.

clue.text: … to make a claim

parts.note: marking out ground one asserts ownership of

explanation.surface: Continuing on from the previous clue, someone asserts a right.
explanation.walkthrough: Linked by the ellipsis to 8-down: its first word means post, its second free, so this answer is a synonym of 8-down word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlers marked boundaries with posts when registering land, hence the idiom of claiming territory.

clue.text: Damaged by admitting to being married

parts.note: someone admitting to a state says 'I am', contracted to I'm
being married means being paired with a spouse

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that marriage has harmed them.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession reads 'I'm paired'; 'by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired is weakened or spoilt in function.

clue.text: Terrible debts contracted by displaced Croat

indicators.note: a displaced thing is moved from its place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: A refugee from Croatia has run up awful debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' rearranges CROAT into ATROC; 'contracted by' only links, in the sense of debts incurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means shockingly bad or appalling.

clue.text: Kayak in which I once sat crumpled up

definitions.text: Kayak in which I once sat crumpled up

indicators.note: crushed into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being squashed into a small canoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled up' rearranges I ONCE SAT; the whole clue also describes a paddler sitting in a kayak.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures a paddler seated in a small craft, as such a sportsperson is.

clue.text: A feller's 66 foot cutter

parts.note: a chain is an old surveyor's measure of 22 yards, sixty-six feet
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: A lumberjack's very long cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' is one who fells trees, not a chap; the chain is an old British length of 22 yards.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the motorised toothed-loop tool lumberjacks use to cut trees.

clue.text: TUC literally spells redundancy

parts.note: these three letters are a word for slash written in reverse order

explanation.surface: The trade union body warns of job losses.
explanation.walkthrough: TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress; its letters read the other way spell a word for slash, so the clue's abbreviation is that word written back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction in staff or spending lays workers off, making them redundant.

clue.text: Priest and I conclude his feelings are amicable

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to conclude is to end

explanation.surface: A priest and I agree that his attitude is friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fr is short for Father, the title of a Catholic priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion is someone who feels warmly and kindly toward you.

clue.text: Wanted to see a baronet in action

indicators.note: the title is placed inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
a baronet carries the title Sir

explanation.surface: Fans are keen to watch a titled gentleman perform.
explanation.walkthrough: A British baronet is addressed as Sir; 'to see' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one wanted is longed for or coveted.

clue.text: Dostoevsky's novel description of an ass

definitions.meaning: the Russian author's 1869 book about Prince Myshkin
an ass being a fool

explanation.surface: A Russian classic sums up a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The book's title names its naive hero, and a donkey is a byword for a fool.

clue.text: Live daughter in good health

parts.note: well means in good health

explanation.surface: A daughter is alive and healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links; 'Live' is the verb, to reside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside there.

clue.text: Little rascals bivouac amidships

indicators.note: the word for bivouac sits in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: SS, for steamship, is the prefix of ships' names
a bivouac is a temporary camp

explanation.surface: Naughty children set up a tent in the middle of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidships' looks like one nautical word but splits into 'amid' and 'ships'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischievous children are rascals or imps.

clue.text: Manse converted into a smart club

indicators.note: a converted building is altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minister's house is turned into a fashionable club.
explanation.walkthrough: A manse is a Scottish minister's house; 'smart' means clever, not fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: This society admits only members with a very high IQ.

clue.text: Little spirit to run fast

definitions.meaning: a small splash of brandy or whisky
sprint

explanation.definitionFit: A splash of liquor is a small measure, and to sprint is to rush.

clue.text: A pretty serious sort of pain

parts.note: pretty means cute

explanation.surface: A rather severe kind of ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' seems to mean 'rather', but it is the adjective attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute pain is sharp and intense, as opposed to chronic.

clue.text: Where naughty boys stood confronted by a dilemma

definitions.meaning: an old school punishment of facing the wall
trapped with no good way out

explanation.surface: Badly behaved pupils were sent to the angle of the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Misbehaving pupils once faced the wall as punishment, and a person with no escape is trapped.

clue.text: His widow no longer has to keep his dinner hot

definitions.text: His widow no longer has to keep his dinner hot

parts.words: His widow no longer has to keep his dinner hot
parts.note: jokingly reads as a spouse who was always delayed, now deceased

explanation.surface: A wife once waited for a tardy spouse who has now died.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word means both deceased and tardy, so the man who came home too late for dinner is also dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's dead spouse is her deceased partner, while tardy describes one who arrives behind time.
